 X finally lets you clip videos without downloading them or using another app 
 Your favorite video moments are now just a few taps away from going viral. 
 By
 Rachit Agarwal 
 Published November 9, 2026 10:35 PM 
 Save 
 Allegra Jacchia / X 
 It’s clear that X wants to transform itself into an all-in-one video creator platform. After letting people upload long-form videos, including hour-long podcasts, the company recently added a feature that allows users to create reaction videos directly from inside the app.
 Now, X has launched a new feature that lets users clip videos without having to download them first or use outside video editing tools. The best part is that original creators finally get the credit they deserve, and they can even get paid for it.
 What was wrong with clipping on X before?
 Previously, if you wanted to share a moment from someone else’s video, you had to save it, trim it in a separate editing app, and then upload it all over again. Worse, the original creator often got no credit and no money, no matter how many views the clip racked up.
 Introducing Clipping 🎬
Until now, clipping on X meant downloading videos, editing them using outside tools, and reuploading. Original creators often didn’t get credit, and even when a clip went viral, they didn’t earn from it.
Native clipping fixes both sides.
Clippers: clip…
— Allegra Jacchia (@allegrajacchia) November 9, 2026 
 Since each clip now points viewers back to the original video, creators can reach a wider audience and pick up new fans along the way. Through X’s Original Content Rewards program, both the clipper and the creator can also earn money from it.
 How do you clip a video on X?
 There are a few rules. You can only clip pre-recorded videos that run for at least two minutes, and your clip must be between 5 and 60 seconds. It also can’t take up more than 30% of the original, so a two-minute video gives you up to 36 seconds. 
 Recommended Videos 
 Videos over 3 minutes and 20 seconds let you use the entire 60 seconds. Sadly, livestreams can’t be clipped yet, but Allegra Jacchia, Creator Product Lead at X, said that the feature is coming soon.
 It’s coming :)
— Allegra Jacchia (@allegrajacchia) November 9, 2026 
 Making a clip is easy. Tap the Repost icon on a video, select “Clip video,” and drag the trimmer handles to pick your moment. If you go over the 30% limit, X will let you know. Tap “Next,” add your thoughts, and hit “Post.”
 If you used to download and re-upload videos to share clips on X, you can finally skip all that. Now it’s quicker and easier, and you might even get paid for it.

 Feeling lonely? Your Instagram activity might be spilling the secret 
 Your Instagram profile might be revealing more about your emotional well-being than you realize. A new study suggests that everyday activity on the platform, from the pictures you post to the time you spend scrolling, could provide useful clues about how lonely someone feels. 
 Researchers at the University of California, San Diego analyzed Instagram data from 415 college students and discovered that different patterns of online behavior were associated with different types of loneliness.

 First TikTok, now eBay? The UK’s social media crackdown is now after secondhand shopping 
 Even eBay and Vinted aren't safe from the UK's growing social media crackdown 
 The UK's upcoming social media ban for children under 16 could soon extend to an unexpected corner of the internet. The government is now considering including popular secondhand marketplaces like eBay and Vinted in its sweeping restrictions, potentially putting buying and selling used goods in the same regulatory category as scrolling through TikTok or Instagram.
 According to a BBC report, UK Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy confirmed that ministers are seriously considering including the two platforms in the upcoming ban, citing concerns about children's online safety. The reasoning has less to do with shopping itself than with the people children might encounter while doing it.

 Research exposes TikTok’s dark side that lures young girls into the world of adult content 
 It starts with a “get ready with me” video and ends on OnlyFans. 
 For years, social media platforms and YouTube have been criticized for quietly serving explicit material to users. In one of the most recent instances, Meta was found running Instagram ads that promoted child sexual abuse material, some of them featuring AI-generated imagery, and was ordered by the Indian government to take them down. But there are plenty of other ways that sexually explicit material is promoted through seemingly harmless social media apps. The latest addition to this sordid chain of events is TikTok.
 According to research conducted by the UK’s Centre to End All Sexual Exploitation (CEASE) and Australia’s Collective Shout, TikTok has become a funnel for promoting adult content hosted on platforms such as OnlyFans. Titled “The TikTok to OnlyFans Pipeline: How TikTok is promoting, normalising and glamourising the sex industry,” the report is the result of a year-long investigation into how OnlyFans is being normalized on the platform.
